iDEP: Pre-Processing and Exploratory Data Analysis

If this site has contributed to your work, please cite our article:

Ge, S.X., Son, E.W. & Yao, R. iDEP: an integrated web application for differential expression and pathway analysis of RNA-Seq data. BMC Bioinformatics 19, 534 (2018). https://doi.org/10.1186/s12859-018-2486-6

Summary

Read Counts data were analyzed using iDEP v2.5.0. The data was first filtered to remove reads below 0.5 CPM in at least 1 sample. Then the data was transformed with EdgeR using a pseudocount of 4. Missing values were imputed using geneMedian.

After mapping, there are 17186 unique genes in 12 samples. Of the 14245 genes passed filter, 14245 were converted to Ensembl/STRING gene IDs in our database. The remaining 0 genes were kept in the data using original IDs.

if (params$data_file_format == 1) {
  total_counts_ggplot(
    counts_data = processed_data$raw_counts,
    sample_info = params$sample_info,
    type = "RAW",
    plots_color_select = params$plots_color_select
  )
} else {
  cat("Total counts plot requires raw count data (integer read counts). ",
      "Your data was loaded as a normalized/FPKM/TPM expression matrix, which does not have ",
      "meaningful total-count sums per sample.\n")
}


if (params$data_file_format == 1 && !is.null(processed_data$raw_counts)) {
  filtered <- as.data.frame(colSums(processed_data$raw_counts))
  original <- as.data.frame(colSums(params$loaded_data))
  df <- merge(x = original, y = filtered, by = "row.names")
  colnames(df) <- c("Sample", "Total Counts", "Total Counts After Filter")
  df$`Counts Removed` <- df$`Total Counts` - df$`Total Counts After Filter`
  numeric_cols <- setdiff(names(df), "Sample")
  df[numeric_cols] <- lapply(df[numeric_cols], function(col) {
    format(col, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
  })
  knitr::kable(
    df,
    caption = "Total reads per sample before and after filtering."
  )
} else if (params$data_file_format != 1) {
  cat("Read counts table not shown: filtering statistics are only meaningful for raw count data. ",
      "Your data was loaded as a normalized/FPKM/TPM expression matrix.\n")
} else if (is.null(processed_data$raw_counts)) {
  cat("Read counts table not shown: raw counts were not available after pre-processing.\n")
}

Marker Gene Plots

marker_payloads <- marker_gene_plot_payloads(
  expr_matrix = processed_data$data,
  sample_info = params$sample_info,
  raw_counts = processed_data$raw_counts,
  converted_data = params$loaded_data,
  all_gene_info = params$all_gene_info
)

if (length(marker_payloads) == 0) {
  if (is.null(params$all_gene_info) || !"ensembl_gene_id" %in% colnames(params$all_gene_info)) {
    cat("Marker gene plots not shown: gene IDs could not be mapped to Ensembl records. ",
        "Provide Ensembl IDs or standard gene symbols.\n")
  } else {
    cat("Marker gene plots not shown: no marker genes from the reference sets were detected in this dataset.\n")
  }
} else {
  counts_flag <- !is.null(processed_data$raw_counts)
  for (payload in marker_payloads) {
    cat("#### ", payload$description, "\n\n", sep = "")
    plot_obj <- build_gene_expression_plot(
      expr_df = payload$data,
      display_name = payload$display_name,
      palette_name = params$plots_color_select,
      plot_type = "bar",
      data_type = "raw",
      counts_are_counts = counts_flag
    )
    plot_obj <- refine_ggplot2(
      p = plot_obj,
      gridline = params$plot_grid_lines,
      ggplot2_theme = params$ggplot2_theme
    )
    print(plot_obj)
    cat("\n\n")
  }
}

To Reproduce This Report Locally

  1. Install the latest iDEP package (once per machine). All the functions and the Rmarkdown code are downloaded with the package. This pulls in ~355 dependencies and can take up to an hour the first time.
install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("url::https://github.com/orditus-llc/idep-desktop/releases/download/v2.5.0/idep250_2.5.0.tar.gz")

Newer releases are listed at https://github.com/orditus-llc/idep-desktop/releases – use the v* tags, not the desktop-v* ones.

  1. Download the RData file from the Prep tab.

  2. Load the downloaded .RData workspace and render this report directly in R or RStudio:

load("idep_session_YYYY_MM_DD.Rdata")

# Read counts data saves report_params directly; the other input formats wrap
# everything in a single params_r list. This handles both.
if (exists("params_r")) report_params <- params_r$report_params

library(report_params$idep_package, character.only = TRUE)
rmarkdown::render(
  system.file("app/www/RMD", "pre_process_workflow.Rmd", package = report_params$idep_package),
  output_dir = getwd(),
  params = report_params,
  envir = new.env(parent = globalenv())
)

The resulting HTML will reproduce what you see in the Prep tab, using the saved report_params list bundled inside every .RData download.
